items.title: World Labs unveiled a spatial world model
items.oneliner: World Labs' Atlas targets generation, reconstruction, and simulation in one stack. Spatial AI is becoming a platform, not a demo.

items.title: Apple started shipping a stronger Siri
items.oneliner: Apple finally shipped a more capable Siri. The assistant race is moving from demos to default interfaces.

items.title: MIT proposed hard constraints for AI safety
items.oneliner: MIT says HardFlow hit perfect constraint satisfaction. Safety work is getting more engineering-grade and less aspirational.

items.title: A single prompt can break alignment
items.oneliner: GRP-Obliteration reportedly unaligns models with one unlabeled prompt. Post-training safety remains far more brittle than vendors admit.

items.title: OpenAI contractors reviewed ChatGPT conversations
items.oneliner: Project Lily confirms humans reviewed real ChatGPT chats. Enterprise buyers should reread every data handling assumption.

items.title: A tool checks residential proxy exposure
items.oneliner: Have I Been Proxied lets teams test whether their IP appears in residential proxy networks. That is useful fraud telemetry.

items.title: Nvidia is formalizing agent permission control
items.oneliner: Nvidia's OpenShell uses formal proofs to bound agent policy changes. Agent governance is finally getting real control planes.

items.title: Inference hardware became the main battleground
items.oneliner: IEEE says 2026 is the inference hardware pivot. Serving tokens cheaply now matters more than training prestige.

items.title: OpenArm lowered the cost of robot research
items.oneliner: OpenArm offers a 7DOF bimanual research platform for $6,500. Physical AI experimentation is getting materially more accessible.

items.title: TSA put an agent into production
items.oneliner: TSA's Ace handles 100,000 traveler conversations monthly and resolves 96% routinely. This is what enterprise agent deployment looks like.
